aks_blog.title: Reducing AKS cold starts with Prepared Image Specification
aks_blog.summary: Have you ever watched your Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) cluster add nodes right on cue, only to wait several more minutes before any of them could take traffic? Or kept extra nodes running all day so a traffic spike wouldn't leave you waiting on cold starts? If large container images or runtime dependencies are making your scale-outs slow and your bill bigger, this post is for you.

aks_releases.title: Release 2026-10-25
aks_releases.body:
## Release Notes - 2026-10-25

> Monitor the release status by regions at [AKS-Release-Tracker](https://releases.aks.azure.com/). This release is titled `v20261025`.

### Announcements of upcoming changes and retirements

* Starting on June 1, 2027, AKS automatically upgrades any cluster that stays on an unsupported Kubernetes version after its 60-day [platform support grace period](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/aks/platform-initiated-upgrades#platform-support-grace-period) ends.
  * What’s changing: AKS will be able to automatically initiate upgrades to help keep clusters supported, secure, and aligned with platform lifecycle requirements.
  * How to prepare now: Review upgrade channels, maintenance windows, and workload readiness so your clusters can absorb automated upgrade events with minimal disruption. See: [Platform-initiated upgrades](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/aks/platform-initiated-upgrades).
* Starting with Kubernetes 1.38, node pools that use the `Ubuntu` OS SKU will default to Ubuntu 26.04. To continue using Ubuntu 24.04 on Kubernetes 1.38, specify the `Ubuntu2404` OS SKU. For more information, see [Upgrade the OS version for your AKS node pools](https://aka.ms/aks/upgrade-os-version).

### Release notes

#### Kubernetes versions

* Kubernetes version [1.37](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.37.md) is now generally available and designated as a [Long-Term Support (LTS)](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/aks/supported-kubernetes-versions?tabs=azure-cli#long-term-support-lts) version. Kubernetes 1.36 is now the default version for new clusters.
* Kubernetes patch versions [1.37.1](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.37.md), [1.36.5](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.36.md), [1.35.9](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.35.md), and [1.34.12](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.34.md) are now available.
* Community support for Kubernetes version [1.34](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.34.md) and LTS support for Kubernetes version [1.31](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.31.md) are going soon end of life by November 2026. Please review the [calendar and platform support policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/aks/supported-kubernetes-versions?tabs=azure-cli#aks-kubernetes-release-calendar-and-upcoming-versions).

More information on supported versions and version support policy is available in [documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/aks/supported-kubernetes-versions?tabs=azure-cli#kubernetes-version-support-policy).

#### Features

* [Node Auto Provisioning (NAP)](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/aks/node-auto-provisioning) now supports the following capabilities:
  * [Capacity Reservation Groups](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/aks/use-capacity-reservation-groups).
  * The Capacity Buffers CRD, which specifies a fixed number of surplus nodes.
  * OS disk type selection with the `osDiskType` field in the `AKSNodeClass` CRD.
  * [Pinning the current node image version and specifying Kubernetes versions](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/aks/node-auto-provisioning-upgrade-image).
  * [Trusted Launch](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/aks/node-autoprovision-aksnodeclass#enable-trusted-launch-in-nap-clusters) through the `AKSNodeClass` CRD.
  * [Azure Container Linux](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/aks/node-autoprovision-aksnodeclass#image-family-configuration) as the node OS.
  * [Managed GPU](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/aks/aks-managed-gpu-nodes), enabled with a field in the `AKSNodeClass` CRD.
* [Node Auto Provisioning (NAP)](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/aks/node-autoprovision) will now have the following changes:
  * Instance-level public IPs with the `spec.nodePublicIP` field in the `AKSNodeClass` CRD.
  * VM SKUs within about six months of retirement are no longer selected for new nodes. See [document](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/virtual-machines/sizes/lifecycle/retirements-and-capacity-restrictions) for details.
  * NAP-enabled clusters now include an AKS-managed `aksmanagednap` node pool, which represents NAP machines through the Machine API for better integration with other AKS features. See the [Azure Karpenter Provider github issue](https://github.com/Azure/karpenter-provider-azure/issues/2032) for more details.
  * When `osDiskSizeGB` isn't specified, the default OS disk size now matches AKS behavior, including SKU-appropriate ephemeral disk sizing where supported.
  * Before choosing an ephemeral disk, NAP now checks eligible disk placements and accounts for Trusted Launch storage needs, preventing failed provisioning.
  * NAP now respects external load balancer exclusions when deciding whether to add nodes to external load balancers.

#### Preview features

* [Windows node support for Node Auto Provisioning (NAP)](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/aks/node-autoprovision-aksnodeclass) is now available in preview. Supports Windows Server 2022 and Windows Server 2025 nodes; Cilium isn't supported on Windows nodes.
* [IPv4/IPv6 Dualstack support in Node Auto Provisioning (NAP) managed clusters](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/aks/node-auto-provisioning-networking#dual-stack-networking-considerations-for-nap-preview) is now available in preview.
* [Updating node public IP prefixes](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/aks/use-node-public-ips) on existing node pools is now available as preview in public Azure regions. Supports adding, replacing, and reordering IPv4 and IPv6 prefixes; changing prefixes recreates the affected nodes. Not yet available in sovereign clouds.
* [Converting AKS Base clusters to AKS Automatic](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/aks/automatic/aks-automatic-sku-migration) with managed system node pools is now available as preview. See [document](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/aks/automatic/aks-automatic-sku-migration) for details.

#### Behavioral changes

* [Istio Gateway API ConfigMap customization](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/aks/istio-gateway-api#configmap-customizations) now supports Service `spec.ports` and Deployment seccomp profile settings for the Istio add-on and Application Routing with Istio.
* [Istio-based service mesh add-on](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/aks/istio-about) will now intercept both IPv4 and IPv6 workload traffic on dual-stack clusters. Restart existing workloads after the add-on update to apply the new proxy configuration.
* [Application Routing Gateway API](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/aks/app-routing-gateway-api) controller will now run on the managed system node pool in AKS Automatic clusters, improving isolation between the control plane and data plane.
* [[AKS Automatic](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/aks/intro-aks-automatic)](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/aks/intro-aks-automatic) clusters on Kubernetes 1.36+ now exclude protected system namespaces from customer mutating admission configurations to preserve the AKS Automatic security boundary: customer webhooks and policies can still mutate customer workloads, but they can’t mutate AKS-managed system workloads.
* [Platform-managed keys for etcd encryption](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/aks/kms-data-encryption?pivots=pmk) will now be enabled by default for new clusters on Kubernetes 1.37 and later, unless infrastructure encryption is explicitly configured.
* [Azure Policy for Kubernetes](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/governance/policy/concepts/policy-for-kubernetes) can now evaluate DELETE operations on Kubernetes resources for policies that explicitly opt in. Existing policies don't enforce DELETE operations.
* [Prepared Image Specification (preview)](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/aks/prepared-image-specificatio

aks_releases.title: Release Notes 2026-09-25
aks_releases.body:
## Release Notes 2026-09-25

> Monitor the release status by regions at [AKS-Release-Tracker](https://releases.aks.azure.com/). This release is titled `v20260925`.

### Announcements of upcoming changes and retirements

* Starting September 30, 2026, AKS will automatically migrate deprecated Availability Sets (VMAS) clusters to Virtual Machines node pools through the auto-upgrader. To control the migration timing, migrate before that date by using `az aks update --migrate-vmas-to-vms`.
* Windows Server 2022 is not supported in kubernetes version 1.37 and above. For more information on this retirement, see the [Retirement GitHub issue](https://github.com/Azure/AKS/issues/4168).

### Release notes

#### Features

* [Identity bindings](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/aks/identity-bindings-concepts), which extends the existing workload identity feature to address scale limitations around federated identity credentials (FICs) on user-assigned managed identities (UAMIs), is now generally available.

#### Preview features

* [Ubuntu 26.04](https://aka.ms/aks/upgrade-os-version) is now available in preview on AKS, using Ubuntu Minimal as the baseline image for Kubernetes 1.36 and later. Register the `Ubuntu2604Preview` flag and use `--os-sku Ubuntu2604` to test the new OS version on supported Generation 2 VM sizes.
* [Windows Server OS SKU migration](https://aka.ms/aks/upgrade-windows-os-version) is now supported in preview to migrate from Windows Server 2022 to Windows Server 2025. On Kubernetes versions where both OS versions are supported, use a node pool update command to migrate. This triggers an automatic reimage.

#### Behavioral changes

* Flatcar Container Linux node images are now removed, causing scaling and remediation (reimage and redeploy) operations to fail. For more information, see [Flatcar preview retirement](https://aka.ms/aks/flatcar-preview-retirement).
* On Kubernetes 1.37, external `LoadBalancer` Services that specify an invalid or non-public load balancer IP address now fail validation early. This provides a clearer error instead of attempting to locate a matching Azure public IP. For more information, see the [Cloud Provider Azure release notes](https://cloud-provider-azure.sigs.k8s.io/blog/2026/09/24/v1.37.0/).
* The `service.beta.kubernetes.io/azure-pip-tags` annotation no longer overrides public IP tags managed by the cloud controller manager, including `k8s-azure-cluster-name`, `k8s-azure-service`, and `k8s-azure-dns-label-service`. Attempts to set these keys, including case variants, are ignored and generate an `IgnoredPIPTagKeys` warning event. This change is included in the [Cloud Provider Azure 1.36.6](https://cloud-provider-azure.sigs.k8s.io/blog/2026/09/14/v1.36.6/) and [1.37.0](https://cloud-provider-azure.sigs.k8s.io/blog/2026/09/24/v1.37.0/) updates.
* AKS now rejects customer-supplied `kubernetes.azure.com/managedby` and `control-plane` values on AKS platform-owned namespace keys. These keys are reserved for AKS; other valid customer-defined labels remain supported.
* AKS release order has been updated: Central US moves to batch 3 while East US moves to batch 6. This change affects release order and timing only. Please check [AKS Release Tracker](https://releases.aks.azure.com/AKSRelease) for details.

#### Bug fixes

* Fixed an issue that allowed an incompatible Capacity Reservation Group (CRG) from the same subscription to be attached to an existing node pool. AKS now checks location and explicit availability-zone compatibility before saving the association. Incompatible configurations fail immediately instead of causing repeated provisioning failures. Regional or automatically zoned VMSS pools must be scaled to zero before attaching a CRG.
* Fixed an issue where CoreDNS replicas could be placed on the same node after a rolling update. On Kubernetes 1.27 and later, updated scheduling constraints spread replicas more evenly across available nodes, improving DNS resilience.
* Fixed an issue where workload identity webhook pods did not restart after a certificate-only update, preventing them from loading the updated certificate.
* Fixed an issue where node image upgrades could use bootstrap settings associated with a previously selected node image instead of the new image.
* Fixed an issue where automatic security patching could repeatedly reimage a node pool that was already running the latest available node image, causing unnecessary disruption and delaying updates to other pools.
* Fixed an issue where upgrades on VMSS-based nodepools could leave extra surge nodes behind when drain-failure recovery had already removed one of the original surge nodes.
* Fixed an issue where configuring a versionless customer-managed key could override an explicitly configured infrastructure encryption setting. AKS now preserves the selected setting. For more information, see [KMS infrastructure encryption](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/aks/migrate-key-management-service-platform-managed-key-customer-managed-key).
* Fixed an incorrect Azure CLI flag in the error message shown when a PodDisruptionBudget blocks node pool deletion. The message now recommends `az aks nodepool delete --ignore-pdb`.

#### Component updates

* Cloud Provider Azure components, including `cloud-controller-manager` and `cloud-node-manager`, have been updated:
  * [`v1.31.15-1`](https://cloud-provider-azure.sigs.k8s.io/blog/2026/09/14/v1.31.15/) on Kubernetes 1.31.
  * [`v1.32.21-1`](https://cloud-provider-azure.sigs.k8s.io/blog/2026/09/14/v1.32.21/) on Kubernetes 1.32.
  * [`v1.33.18-1`](https://cloud-provider-azure.sigs.k8s.io/blog/2026/09/14/v1.33.18/) on Kubernetes 1.33.
  * [`v1.34.14-1`](https://cloud-provider-azure.sigs.k8s.io/blog/2026/09/14/v1.34.14/) on Kubernetes 1.34.
  * [`v1.35.9-1`](https://cloud-provider-azure.sigs.k8s.io/blog/2026/09/14/v1.35.9/) on Kubernetes 1.35.
  * [`v1.36.6-1`](https://cloud-provider-azure.sigs.k8s.io/blog/2026/09/14/v1.36.6/) on Kubernetes 1.36.
  * [`v1.37.0-1`](https://cloud-provider-azure.sigs.k8s.io/blog/2026/09/24/v1.37.0/) on Kubernetes 1.37 and later.
  * Windows `cloud-node-manager` uses the corresponding `-windows-hpc-1` builds. The health probe proxy has been updated to `v1.36.6-1`.
* Azure CNI and CNS have been updated to [`v1.8.13`](https://github.com/Azure/azure-container-networking/releases/tag/v1.8.13) for Kubernetes 1.35.
* Azure CSI drivers have been updated:
  * Azure File CSI driver to [`v1.34.10`](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/azurefile-csi-driver/releases/tag/v1.34.10) on Kubernetes 1.34 and [`v1.35.10`](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/azurefile-csi-driver/releases/tag/v1.35.10) on Kubernetes 1.35 and later.
  * Azure Blob CSI driver to [`v1.27.11`](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/blob-csi-driver/releases/tag/v1.27.11) on Kubernetes 1.34 and later.
  * Azure Disk CSI driver to [`v1.33.13`](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/azuredisk-csi-driver/releases/tag/v1.33.13) on Kubernetes 1.34, [`v1.34.7`](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/azuredisk-csi-driver/releases/tag/v1.34.7) on Kubernetes 1.35 and 1.36, and [`v1.36.0`](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/azuredisk-csi-driver/releases/tag/v1.36.0) on Kubernetes 1.37 and later.
* Secrets Store CSI Driver has been updated to [`v1.5.7`](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/secrets-store-csi-driver/releases/tag/v1.5.7).
* The KEDA add-on has been updated to [`2.20.2`](https://github.com/kedacore/keda/releases/tag/v2.20.2) for Kubernetes 1.37. Kubernetes 1.36 and earlier retain their existing KEDA versions.
* Ratify has been updated to [`v1.4.6`](https://github.com/notaryproject/ratify/releases/tag/v1.4.6).
* Tigera Operator has been updated to [`v1.40.15-4`](https://github.com/tigera/operator/releases/tag/v1.40.15).
* Istio-based service mesh add-on revisions `asm-1-29` and `asm-1-30` have been updated to security-patched builds [`1.29.7-2`](https://github.com/istio/istio/releases/tag

behavioral_changes.title: [AKS Automatic
behavioral_changes.summary: ](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/aks/intro-aks-automatic) clusters on Kubernetes 1.36+ now exclude protected system namespaces from customer mutating admission configurations to preserve the AKS Automatic security boundary: customer webhooks and policies can still mutate customer workloads, but they can’t mutate AKS-managed system workloads.
